en: The Sutra on Śāriputra’s Repentance, spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha together with twelve hundred and fifty [monks].
A thousand bhikṣu-bodhisattvas were seated together.
The foremost disciple, Śāriputra, rose from his seat, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and asked the Buddha:
"If there are good men or good women who desire to seek the path of the Buddha, yet have committed evil in previous lives, how should they repent for it?"
The Buddha said,
"Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra!"
"I am concerned that the gods and humans are so fond of this.
The Buddha said:

"If there are good men or good women who wish to seek the path of an Arhat, who wish to seek the path of a Pratyekabuddha, who wish to seek the path of a Buddha, or who wish to know the matters of the past and future, they should always—at dawn, midday, sunset, the hour of midnight, midnight, and at cockcrow—wash and rinse their mouths, adjust their robes, join their palms in worship, and pay homage to the ten directions."
In whatever direction one turns, one should repent with these words:

"We have committed transgressions and evils since countless kalpas in our past lives; throughout this present life, we have committed acts of lust, anger, and folly. We did not know the proper time for the Buddha, nor the proper time for the Dharma, nor the proper time for the Saṃgha of bhikṣus, nor the proper time for what is wholesome and unwholesome."

If one commits an offense with the body, or commits an offense with speech, or commits an offense with the mind, or commits an offense with the intention; or if one intends to harm the Buddha, harbors malice toward the sutras and the Way, engages in strife with the Sangha of bhikṣus, kills an arhat, or kills one's own father or mother.
If one commits the three offenses of body, the four of speech, and the three of mind—personally killing living beings, inciting others to kill, or seeing others kill and rejoicing in their place;
personally committing theft, inciting others to steal, or seeing others steal and rejoicing in their place;
personally deceiving others, inciting others to deceive, or seeing others deceive and rejoicing in their place; [one is bound by these transgressions].
One personally engages in divisive speech, teaches others to engage in divisive speech, and rejoices when seeing others engaging in divisive speech;
one personally engages in verbal abuse, teaches others to engage in verbal abuse, and rejoices when seeing others engaging in verbal abuse;
one personally engages in false speech, teaches others to engage in false speech, and rejoices when seeing others engaging in false speech.
One is personally jealous and envious; one teaches others to be jealous and envious; seeing others being jealous and envious, one rejoices on their behalf.
One is personally greedy and covetous; one teaches others to be greedy and covetous; seeing others being greedy and covetous, one rejoices on their behalf.
One is personally faithless; one teaches others not to have faith; seeing others being faithless, one rejoices on their behalf.
In one's own person, one does not believe that performing good brings good and committing evil brings evil; seeing others commit evil, one rejoices in it on their behalf.
In one's own person, one steals divine objects from Buddhist temples or the property of the bhikṣu-saṃgha; one teaches others to steal; seeing others steal, one rejoices in it on their behalf.

In one's own person, one uses light weights, small pecks, and short measures to deceive others, while using heavy weights, large pecks, and long measures to encroach upon others; seeing others encroach upon others, one rejoices in it on their behalf.
One commits intentional murder oneself, incites others to commit intentional murder, or seeing others commit intentional murder, rejoices in their behalf;
one commits evil and rebellious acts oneself, incites others to commit evil and rebellious acts, or seeing others commit evil and rebellious acts, rejoices in their behalf.

Regarding all the transgressions committed throughout successive births in the five realms of existence—namely, while dwelling in the hells, among animals, as hungry ghosts (preta), or among humans—these include failing to be filial toward one’s parents, failing to be filial toward one’s teachers, failing to respect virtuous friends, failing to respect virtuous śramaṇas and practitioners, and failing to respect elders; as well as treating one’s parents with contempt, treating one’s teachers and preceptors with contempt, treating those who seek the path of an Arhat with contempt, treating those who seek the path of a Pratyekabuddha with contempt, or slandering and envying them.

To perceive the Buddha-way as wrong, to perceive the evil paths as right, to perceive what is correct as incorrect, and to perceive what is incorrect as correct— whatever transgressions and evils we have committed,

we pray that the Buddhas of the ten directions will take pity on us and accept our repentance, so that we may not incur these faults and calamities in this present life, and that we may likewise not suffer these faults and calamities in future lives.
Why do we seek the compassion of the Buddhas of the ten directions?
Because the Buddhas possess the power of penetrating vision and hearing, none dare to deceive them.
We have no intention of concealing our transgressions and evils; from this day forward, we shall not commit them again.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"If there are good sons or good daughters who do not wish to enter the hells, the realm of animals, or the realm of hungry ghosts (preta), they should repent for all the transgressions they have committed and must not conceal them; after receiving the precepts, they must not commit evil again."

Those who do not wish to be born in border regions where there is no Buddha, where there are no sutras, where there is no community of bhikṣus, where there is no righteous principle, or where there is no distinction between good and evil, should all repent their transgressions and must not conceal them.

One should not desire to be foolish, deaf, blind, or mute; nor should one desire to be born as a butcher, a fisherman, a hunter, a jailer, or into a poor household. One must repent for all such transgressions and must not conceal them.
Women who desire to seek out men should all repent their transgressions.
Those who wish to attain the stage of Srotāpanna and no longer enter the realms of hell or hungry ghosts should all repent their transgressions.

Those who wish to attain the stage of Sakṛdāgāmin and be reborn among the gods above; those who wish to attain the stage of Anāgāmin and be reborn among the twenty-four heavens above; those who wish to attain Arhatship and enter parinirvāṇa; those who wish to attain the path of Arhatship within this world; those who wish to attain the path of a Pratyekabuddha; and those who wish to know the matters of the past and future—all must repent their transgressions and must not conceal them.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“If there are good men or good women who, each day at the three times, prostrate themselves and pay homage to all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions.”
The Buddhas of the ten directions all employ the impartial and correct teaching to instruct the people of the world; wherever the sun and moon shine, they cause the populace to perform good deeds.
The Buddha rains down the path of the sutras upon the world, just as when it rains from heaven, the hundred grains and all vegetation flourish and thrive.

The Buddha rains down the teachings of the sutras upon the world; therefore, there arise feudal lords and kings, the Four Heavenly Kings, and ascending as far as the thirty-three heavens, where beings are noble, wealthy, and enjoy happiness.
O Buddhas who have brought forth those who have attained the stage of Srotāpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, and Arhat, we pray that all the Buddhas of the ten directions will listen to what we say:

"Regarding the good and evil deeds performed by the people of the world and the various classes of crawling and flying creatures—whether they practice giving, uphold the Way with diligence without violating the sutras and precepts, maintain a heart of compassion toward the people, perform immeasurable acts of goodness, give to Bodhisattvas and the community of bhikṣus, or give to ordinary people and the poor, even down to showing mercy and pity to birds and beasts—we [the donors] exhort them to do good and assist them in their joy."
Regarding all the people whom the Buddhas of the past have delivered and caused to attain *nirvāṇa*, we [the undersigned] all rejoice in their behalf.

Regarding all those whom the Buddhas of the future will teach to perform good deeds and distance themselves from the five evils and the path of birth and death, leading them to attain the way of the *arhat* or *pratyekabuddha*, we [the undersigned] all encourage and delight them, causing them to do good and become like the Buddha.

Regarding those currently to be delivered by the Buddhas of the present in the ten directions, we shall instruct people to practice generosity and not violate the sutras and precepts, and to show compassion toward all people and even the smallest crawling insects. We shall cause them all to be liberated from the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, and the ignorance of poverty; furthermore, we shall lead them to attain the paths of *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, *arhat*, *pratyekabuddha*, and *nirvāṇa*. We, [the undersigned], shall all exhort and encourage them to perform good deeds and assist them in their joy.

All those bodhisattvas of the past who had not yet attained buddhahood practiced the six pāramitās to perform wholesome deeds: they practiced the dāna-pāramitā of giving; they practiced the śīla-pāramitā of not violating the prohibitions of the Path; they practiced the kṣānti-pāramitā of patience; they practiced the vīrya-pāramitā of diligence; they practiced the dhyāna-pāramitā of single-mindedness; and they practiced the prajñā-pāramitā of wisdom, thereby perfecting the six pāramitās.
Regarding all bodhisattvas of the past who have practiced the six pāramitās, we exhort them, encourage them, and assist them in their joy.
Regarding all bodhisattvas of the future who will practice the six pāramitās, we exhort them, encourage them, and assist them in their joy.
Regarding those Bodhisattvas currently practicing the six *pāramitās*, we [the undersigned] exhort them, encourage them, and assist them in their joy.

Whatever merit we have obtained, we dedicate it all to the people of the ten directions throughout the world—our parents, the crawling and wriggling creatures, those with two feet, those with four feet, and those with many feet—so that they may all attain Buddhahood.

“The merit of a person who attains Pratyekabuddhahood and uses the gold, silver, and treasures of four great cities as an offering would be a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, and even a hundred-millionfold greater.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“If there is a son of good family or a daughter of good family who, throughout the day and night, should three times each prostrate themselves and pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions, saying:”
"May you grant us an audience for what we have to say.

Although the Buddhas of the ten directions, having already attained Buddhahood, do not preach the sutras, we now exhort them to preach the sutras for the sake of the devas and humans, and for all classes of sentient beings, including those that fly and those that crawl, so that they may be liberated from the realms of hell, animals, hungry ghosts, ignorance, and poverty, and ultimately attain the path of Nirvāṇa."

"O you who in the ten directions desire to enter parinirvāṇa, we pray that you will grant us your compassion and not yet enter parinirvāṇa; you should cause all devas, humans, and even the smallest crawling insects to obtain merit, and enable them all to be liberated from the realms of hell and hungry ghosts."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“In our past lives when we were bodhisattvas, we exhorted and encouraged all Buddhas to preach the sutras, saying, ‘Please do not enter parinirvāṇa yet.’”
For this reason, we have become Buddhas.

Now that the first of the Four Heavenly Kings and the second heavenly king, Śakra, have descended and joined their palms in prostration, beseeching us with compassion, we shall protect all the devas and people while preaching this sutra.
"Countless devas have exhorted me, saying: 'Do not yet enter parinirvāṇa.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"In this way, among these people, each receives their lot according to their kind; those who do good obtain their own blessings, and those who do evil obtain their own calamities."
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If there are good men or good women who wish to seek the path of the Buddha, by what vow should they act so as to attain it?”
The Buddha said:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who, during each of the three periods of day and night, prostrate themselves and address the Buddhas of the ten directions, saying:
'May the Buddhas of the ten directions listen!'"

We, [Name] and others, have accumulated merit since time immemorial, throughout incalculable kalpas—whether through giving alms, upholding the Way of the Sūtras, maintaining a benevolent mind, performing good deeds for the Buddha, performing good deeds for the Sūtras, performing good deeds for the Bhikṣu Saṃgha, performing good deeds for ordinary people, or performing both good and evil deeds toward birds and beasts. For such evil deeds, we ourselves receive their calamities; for such good deeds, we ourselves receive their blessings. Having performed evil, we now repent of it ourselves.

To uphold the sutras and precepts without violating them; if one has received the precepts, not to engage in sexual intercourse with women; to encourage all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the myriad people to perform good deeds; and to exhort all Buddhas not to enter parinirvāṇa yet.

We take all the merit and virtue we have acquired since beginning our study of the Way and gather it together; with a sincere heart, we bestow it upon the people and parents of the ten directions throughout the world, as well as upon all classes of beings, from those that fly and crawl, so that all may obtain its blessings.

There are others who have received but little; may they cause me to attain it. May they cause me and my peers to practice the path of the Buddha as taught in the Buddhist scriptures. Those who have not yet been delivered, we shall deliver them; those who have not yet been liberated, we and our peers shall liberate them; those who have not yet attained nirvāṇa, we and our peers shall cause them to attain nirvāṇa.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Suppose all the men and women in the world were to become arhats and pratyekabuddhas.
If someone were to make offerings to all those arhats and pratyekabuddhas in the world for a thousand years, would their merit not be great?"

Śāriputra said: "If one were to make offerings to a single arhat or pratyekabuddha for a single day, the merit thereof would be immeasurable; how much more so if one were to do so for a thousand years to all the arhats and pratyekabuddhas throughout the world?"
The Buddha said:

“To provide offerings for the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas of the world for a thousand years is not as good as reciting the *Sūtra on Repentance* three times each day and night for a single day; the merit one thereby obtains surpasses that of offering to the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas of the world by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, and a hundred-millionfold.”
The Sūtra on Śāriputra’s Repentance Spoken by the Buddha
